title: The travelling salesman tour of a sunflower
statement: The sunflower point set S_N consists of the points k = 1, ..., N at (round(1000 sqrt(k) cos(k a)), round(1000 sqrt(k) sin(k a))), with the golden angle a = pi (3 - sqrt 5) (Vogel's model of the florets of a sunflower head); the coordinates are fixed in collections/originals/instances/sunflower-N.txt. The distance between two points is their Euclidean distance rounded to the nearest integer (TSPLIB EUC_2D). Find the shortest closed tour through all points of S_10000. Best known: 17,245,349 (ours); no lower bound has been computed.
submission: Text file: the point numbers 1..10000 in the order of the tour, each exactly once (one per line or separated by spaces).
score: the tour length in rounded Euclidean distances, an integer (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: nearest-neighbour start, 2-opt and Or-opt with 10-nearest-neighbour lists, then 5 minutes of segment perturbation (tools/src/tsp2opt.c)

context: Benchmark sets for the travelling salesman problem are mostly random uniform points, clustered points or real cities (TSPLIB, the DIMACS challenge, the national instances), and the best solvers (Concorde for proofs, LKH for tours) are tuned on them. The sunflower is a deterministic, quasi-uniform point set with a different geometry: points lie on families of crossing spirals (parastichies whose counts are Fibonacci numbers), the density is uniform on average but the local structure changes slowly with the radius. How the optimal tour follows these spirals, and how its length compares with the Beardwood-Halton-Hammersley asymptotics for random points (constant 12 of the optimization-constants repository), are open; the instance is defined exactly and every tour is checked in integer arithmetic.
references: H. Vogel, A better way to construct the sunflower head, Mathematical Biosciences 44 (1979) 179-189
G. Reinelt, TSPLIB - a traveling salesman problem library, ORSA J. Computing 3 (1991) 376-384 (EUC_2D distances)
D. Applegate, R. Bixby, V. Chvatal, W. Cook, The Traveling Salesman Problem: A Computational Study (Princeton, 2006)

novelty.verdict: new. The sunflower (golden-angle spiral) point set does not appear among the TSP benchmark sets or in any paper found on arXiv or the web, and the instance here is defined by us.
closest: TSPLIB and the DIMACS TSP challenge instances (random, clustered and geographic point sets); none is a phyllotactic spiral.
novelty.benchmark: the benchmark has vehicle routing (CVRPLIB) instances, not the travelling salesman problem on this point set

first_values.note: Both found with tools/src/tsp2opt.c (10 s for N = 1000, 300 s for N = 10000); upper bounds only. The N = 1000 instance is in instances/sunflower-1000.txt and can be checked with the same checker.

baseline.text: 17,245,349 for N = 10000, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the tour in `refs/tsp-sunflower.txt`. This is a quick local-search tour; a stronger heuristic (Lin-Kernighan type) should improve it, and an exact solver could settle the optimum.
